english.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial choice when something is unsuitable or simply wrong.
This is the all-purpose casual choice for something that is not suitable or not right.
Use this when something is not right, suitable, or appropriate rather than simply factually false.

examples.english: This outfit is improper for me to wear to work.
examples.jyutping: nei1 gin6 saam1 m4 ngaam1 ngo5 faan1 gung1 zoek3

examples.english: This shirt is unsuitable for me.
examples.jyutping: ni1 gin6 saam1 ngo5 zoek6 soeng5 san1 m4 ngaam1

examples.english: This outfit is incorrect for the occasion.
examples.jyutping: ni1 tou3 saam1 m4 ngaam1 ni1 go3 coeng4 hap6

english.note: Use this for an answer, claim, or detail that is simply incorrect rather than merely imprecise.
Use this when something is wrong, inappropriate, or does not seem right.
Use 唔啱 when something is wrong, unsuitable, or inappropriate rather than merely generally bad.

examples.english: Your answer is inaccurate; try again.
examples.traditional: 你個答案唔啱，試多次啦。
examples.jyutping: nei5 go3 daap3 on3 m4 ngaam1 si3 do1 ci3 laa1
ni1 go3 daap3 on3 m4 ngaam1 wo3

examples.english: Your answer is bad—it is incorrect.
examples.jyutping: nei5 go3 daap3 on3 m4 ngaam1 wo3

english.note: Use 唔啱 when “wrong” means morally not right or inappropriate rather than factually incorrect.

examples.english: Talking to elderly people like that is wrong.
examples.traditional: 咁樣對老人家講嘢好唔啱。
examples.jyutping: gam2 joeng2 deoi3 lou5 jan4 gaa1 gong2 je5 hou2 m4 ngaam1
